name: Whiteface Mountain
operator: New York State Olympic Regional Development Authority (ORDA)

Piste reference data (not web-verified in this build) — confirm at source. Advertised figures: 1,220 ft base, 3,430 ft vertical measured to the top of hike-to terrain (~4,650 ft). The lift-served top is ~4,386 ft (1,337 m), used for the summit weather point

character: A state-owned Adirondack ski mountain near Lake Placid, run by ORDA, with one of the largest vertical drops in the eastern US and steep, often wind-exposed upper terrain. It hosted the alpine events of the 1980 Winter Olympics.
learning: Reference note: beginner terrain and lessons are concentrated at the Bear Den area near the main base, away from the steep upper mountain. Confirm current learning lifts and lesson programs.

season.notes: No 2026-27 opening or closing date found in research as of 2026-09-28. ORDA announced its 2025-26 opening dates for Belleayre, Gore and Whiteface only on 2025-11-21 (see the ORDA release in More links), so 2026-27 dates may not appear until around November 2026. The 2025-26 Whiteface date itself and past actual opening dates were not captured.

driveFromIthaca.basis: Estimate from typical routing (NY-13/I-81 N to Watertown, NY-3 E via Cranberry Lake and Tupper Lake to Saranac Lake, then NY-86 through Lake Placid to Wilmington); not a routing-service result. Alternatives via I-88/I-87 N to Exit 30 and NY-73, or via Utica and NY-28/NY-30, take similar time; Adirondack winter roads can add significant time.
